title: Nyla Inc escalation: unblock continuous-batcher freeze under mixed-length heavy tails
creator: Leila Morgan
description:
Summary: Nyla Inc reported repeated production outages in Hosted and Dedicated deployments over the last three weeks where the continuous batching subsystem would 'freeze' for 30s-90s intervals. Affected endpoints were low-latency chat routes (short requests) that suddenly experienced orders-of-magnitude tail latency. Private customers with similar traffic patterns reported a correlated increase in long-context tail latency but were able to mitigate via manual ingress throttling.

Observed behavior:
- Ingest burst of mixed-length requests (many short init messages interleaved with a few long-context completions) triggered a chain where the adaptive admission reservoir favored long requests and prevented small, latency-sensitive requests from being admitted.
- The continuous-batcher built large heterogeneous in-flight batches which caused KV cache churn and repeated eviction waves. Eviction waves amplified queue head-of-line blocking and produced starvation for small request flows.
- Telemetry showed the dispatcher stalled while waiting on KV turns with >95% GPU utilization, but single-token-latency-sensitive flows saw 10x tail latency increases.

Reproduction notes:
- Repro script: scripts/repro/nyla_mixed_burst.py (internal). Pattern: 1200 short requests/sec + 8 concurrent 16k-token requests sustained for 20s.
- Environment: repro in staging-hosted and dedicated-stress. Private customer reproduced locally using the same workload on their on-prem cluster (config differences: older kernel v5.15, different CUDA drivers).

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Interaction between adaptive admission windowing and KV cache eviction heuristics: when long-context requests enter, admission expands to accommodate but continuous-batcher does not maintain strict length-class isolation. The result is repeated heterogeneous batches that cause hot KV entries to be evicted and re-requested, producing a backpressure loop and effective queue starvation of short flows.
- Secondary factor: preemption path latency is higher under heavy KV churn so preemptive dequeueing does not regain fairness quickly enough.

Customer impact and urgency:
- Nyla Inc reported customer-facing errors and SLA violations; engineering support escalated to P0. Several enterprise customers expressed concern about Dedicated capacity predictability. Private customers requested a reproducible mitigation guide.

Mitigation performed so far:
- 2026-02-11: Rolled out a temporary admission cap in hosted (config: max_admit_per_window=400) limiting long-request ramp-up; dropped P95 by ~60% for short flows.
- 2026-02-13: Applied a queue-priority patch in Dedicated clusters to prefer short-token routes for 10% traffic canary.
- 2026-02-15: Provided Private customers with a manual ingress throttling recipe and a monitoring dashboard (Grafana link) to detect impending eviction waves.

Proposed permanent fix (plan):
1) Implement length-class isolation in continuous-batcher: maintain separate admission buckets for short/medium/long and only allow limited co-batching across classes. This avoids heterogeneous batch formation that triggers KV churn.
2) Harden KV cache eviction policy: introduce a short-term pinning mechanism for recently-accessed KV entries used by low-latency flows to avoid immediate eviction during bursts.
3) Improve preemptive-dequeue latency path: optimize lock-free handoff and add fast-path to preempt large requests when starvation for short flows is detected.
4) Expand scheduler guardrails: add adaptive backpressure that triggers earlier and emits high-confidence alerts to console and on-call.
5) Automation: add synthetic test to CI that runs mixed-length stress workloads to prevent regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (Hotfix): Deploy admission cap and priority guard to all Hosted clusters and ramp to Dedicated pools by 2026-03-01. (Done for hosted, 60% for dedicated).
- Stage 2 (Patch): Merge length-class isolation and KV pinning into runtime-1.22; deploy as 10% canary to Hosted on 2026-03-10.
- Stage 3 (Scale): Monitor canary for 72 hours; if stable, rollout to Dedicated and publish Private upgrade pack and Helm chart changes with clear rollback steps.

Testing and observability:
- Added flaggable synthetic scenario in perf harness: perf/batch_mixed_length_scenario.java.
- New dashboards: grafana.redwood.com/d/Batching/nyla-escalation (alerts wired to #oncall and PagerDuty).

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence RCA: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Nyla+Batcher+RCA
- GitHub hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1728 (admission cap + priority guard)
- GitHub RFC for length-class isolation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/54
- Repro script (internal): https://git.internal/redwood/repro/nyla_mixed_burst.py
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/Batching/nyla-escalation

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Isolation strictness vs. batch efficiency: stronger isolation reduces cost efficiency (fewer large homogeneous batches) — product needs to weigh SLA guarantees vs unit-cost increase.
- KV pinning memory pressure: pinning increases cache pressure; need tuning per instance size. Consider a TTL-based pin rather than infinite pin.
- Private upgrade cadence: some Private customers run older drivers/OS kernels; we need a compatibility matrix to avoid regressions on their platforms.

Acceptance criteria:
- No repeat of 30s+ batching freezes for repro workload in staging for 72h.
- Tail latency for short flows returns to baseline (<=1.5x) under mixed-length stress.
- Canary error rates <0.1% and no customer escalations post-rollout for 14 days.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Rafael Kim: implement length-class admission buckets (eng owner) — due 2026-03-08.
- Priya Desai: design KV pin TTL strategy and memory budgeting (eng) — due 2026-03-05.
- Oncall (SRE): maintain hosted admission cap until runtime-1.22 canary is green — ongoing.
- Solutions Eng: coordinate Private customer upgrade plans and provide test harness for customers — due 2026-03-12.
